mainTopic: רב מתנא's dislocated thigh bone, the size of a hole in the windpipe, standing for scholars, and whether 'until' includes the measure
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש read the extra phrases in the משנה. Each uses רב מתנא's case of a thigh bone that slipped out of its socket. Then the גמרא looks at that case directly: רב מתנא says the animal is טרפה, and רבא says it is כשרה unless the sinew is torn. The final הלכה is that it stays כשרה until the sinew decays. Next, זעירי gives the size of the hole in the windpipe using a coin people in בבל knew. A story about רבי יוחנן asking a money changer for that coin leads to a side discussion: workers do not stand up for תלמידי חכמים while working, but they do stand for people bringing ביכורים. Last, רב נחמן rules that an exact measure counts as more than the measure, so 'until' does not include the measure. The גמרא defends this against challenges from a משנה about a rope hanging off a bed, and it begins a new test from a משנה about tiny clay vessels that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How רבי יוחנן explains the phrase 'these are טרפות'
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, the תנא wrote 'אלו טרפות' to keep רב מתנא's case out of the general rule, so that animal is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא saw that someone might put רב מתנא's case under 'this is the principle,' because a slipped-out thigh bone looks like a 'removed' organ. So he wrote 'these are טרפות,' meaning only these are טרפה, and רב מתנא's case is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי יוחנן's view: the words 'אלו טרפות' are meant exactly, and they are there to teach that רב מתנא's case is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule, 'זה הכלל,' could make us think a dislocated thigh bone is טרפה, because it looks like a missing organ (נטולין). To block that mistake, the תנא opened with 'אלו טרפות.' The point is that only the listed cases are טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect; it may not be eaten even after proper שחיטה
Kosher, allowed to be eaten
'This is the principle,' the general rule in the משנה
Organs that are removed or missing (one group of טרפות)
'These are טרפות,' the opening words of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here the case of רב מתנא comes out כשרה only because of how רבי יוחנן reads the משנה. Do not mix this up with רב מתנא's own ruling later on, where he says it is טרפה.

phrases.english: And he saw the case of Rav Mattana
phrases.notes: 'He' means the תנא of the משנה. רב מתנא's case is a thigh bone that slipped out of its socket.

phrases.english: that it would fall under 'this is the principle.'
What is the reason? Because it resembles 'removed' organs.
So he taught 'These are tereifot':
only these are tereifa,
but the case of Rav Mattana is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַזְיַיהּ לִדְרַב מַתְנָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּזֶה הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation, started before this section, of why רבי יוחנן says the משנה needs both phrases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that an extra phrase is there to keep out a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A dislocated thigh bone might count as a missing organ under 'זה הכלל' and be טרפה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אלו טרפות' limits טרפות to the list, so רב מתנא's case is כשרה

steps.title: How ריש לקיש explains the phrase 'these are kosher'
steps.stepSummary: According to ריש לקיש, the תנא wrote 'אלו כשרות' to keep רב מתנא's case out of the kosher group, so that animal is טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says 'these are kosher' is meant exactly. The תנא saw that רב מתנא's case does not fit under 'this is the principle,' because it is not like perforated, cut, or removed organs. So he wrote 'these are kosher,' meaning only these are kosher, and רב מתנא's case is טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives ריש לקיש's opposite reading: the exact phrase is 'אלו כשרות,' and it teaches that רב מתנא's case is טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריש לקיש's reading, the dislocated thigh bone does not match any of the three groups (נקובות, פסוקות, נטולות). So we might think it is כשרה. The words 'אלו כשרות' teach that only the listed cases are כשרה, which makes רב מתנא's case טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Precisely; the words are meant exactly
Organs that are perforated (pierced)
Organs that are cut through, such as the windpipe
'These are kosher,' the list of kosher cases in the next משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש use the same case, רב מתנא's thigh bone, to show which phrase in the משנה is exact. For רבי יוחנן it comes out כשרה; for ריש לקיש it comes out טרפה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
'These are kosher' is meant precisely.
He taught the tereifot, and he taught 'this is the principle,'
and he saw the case of Rav Mattana
that it would not fall under 'this is the principle.'
What is the reason? It is not like perforated organs,
and it is not like cut organs,
and it is also not like removed organs.
So he taught 'These are kosher':
only these are kosher,
but the case of Rav Mattana is tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵלּוּ כְּשֵׁרוֹת דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror-image explanation for ריש לקיש's view
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that an extra phrase is there to keep out a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A dislocated thigh bone fits no group of טרפות, so it would be כשרה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אלו כשרות' limits כשרות to the list, so רב מתנא's case is טרפה

steps.title: רב מתנא and רבא argue about a thigh bone that slipped out of its socket
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא says a thigh bone that slipped out of its socket makes the animal טרפה. רבא says it is כשרה, but if the sinew is torn it is טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself. רב מתנא said: if the top of the thigh bone slips out of its place, the animal is טרפה. רבא said: it is kosher, but if its sinew is torn, it is טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at רב מתנא's statement directly, the one it kept mentioning above. רבא disagrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנא says the dislocation alone makes the animal טרפה. רבא says a dislocation alone is not enough. For him, what makes it טרפה is the tearing of the sinew that holds the bone in place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא goes back to look closely at a statement it quoted earlier
The ball-shaped head of the thigh bone (femur)
Slipped out of its place
Its sinew (the tendon holding the bone in the socket)
Was torn or cut

phrases.english: Back to the matter itself. Rav Mattana said:
This head of the thigh bone
that slipped out of its place: tereifa.
And Rava said: kosher,
but if its sinew is torn: tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to analyze רב מתנא's statement directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב מתנא: dislocation makes the animal טרפה. רבא: dislocation is כשרה, but a torn sinew is טרפה.

steps.title: The final הלכה: kosher until the sinew decays
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that even a torn sinew is כשרה. The animal becomes טרפה only once the sinew has decayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: even if the sinew is torn, it is kosher, until it has completely decayed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling, and it is even more lenient than רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a torn sinew makes the animal טרפה. The הלכה says a torn sinew is still כשרה. Only when the sinew has decayed does the animal become טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling, the practical הלכה
Has completely decayed or rotted away

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a dislocated thigh bone, and even a torn sinew, leave the animal כשרה. It becomes טרפה only when the sinew has decayed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for checking the hind leg of an animal.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: even if it is torn, it is kosher,
until it has completely decayed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument between רב מתנא and רבא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A torn sinew is still כשרה; only a decayed sinew makes the animal טרפה.

steps.title: זעירי explains the size of the hole in the windpipe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's question about how much the windpipe can be missing. זעירי explains the size using a coin known in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'How much can it be missing?' זעירי said: You, who are not familiar with this measure, should think of it as a Kurdish dinar. It is like a small פרוטה, and it can be found among the פרוטות of פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about the windpipe. זעירי explains its measure for people in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measures the hole using an Italian איסר, a coin the people of בבל did not use. זעירי gives them a coin they knew instead: a Kurdish dinar, which is like a small פרוטה found in פומבדיתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The measure or size the הלכה depends on
A Kurdish dinar, a coin known in בבל
A פרוטה, a small coin
The Italian איסר, the coin used as the measure in the משנה

phrases.english: How much can it be missing?
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about the windpipe. There, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers: the size of an Italian איסר.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said:
You, who are not familiar with the measure,
its measure is a Kurdish dinar,
and it is like a small peruta,
and it is found among the perutot of Pumbedita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Italian איסר in the משנה equals a Kurdish dinar, like a small פרוטה of פומבדיתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן tells the money changer to stay seated
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנא the money changer tells how רבי יוחנן asked him for a Kurdish coin to measure טרפות. When he tried to stand up for him, רבי יוחנן said workers may not stand for תלמידי חכמים while they are working.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנא the money changer said: בר נפחא was standing over me and asked me for a Kurdish dinar to measure טרפות. I wanted to stand up for him, but he did not let me. He said: Sit, my son, sit. Workers may not stand up for תלמידי חכמים while they are busy at their work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story connected to זעירי's coin from the last step, and it carries a new rule about standing up for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story links back to the coin used to measure the hole in the windpipe. While it is being told, רבי יוחנן states a rule: a worker on the job should not stop working to stand up for a scholar. This rule becomes the subject of the next few steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A money changer, someone who sits at a table of coins
טרפות, animals with a fatal defect
Craftsmen or workers
Torah scholars

phrases.english: Rabbi Chana the money changer said:

phrases.aramaic: עִילָּא מִינַּאי הֲוָה קָאֵי בַּר נַפָּחָא,
phrases.english: Bar Nappacha was standing over me,
phrases.notes: בר נפחא is a nickname for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: and he asked me for a Kurdish dinar
to measure טרפות with it,
phrases.notes: This is the coin זעירי used in the last step to measure the hole in the windpipe.

phrases.english: and I wanted to stand up before him,
but he did not let me.
He said to me: Sit, my son, sit.
Workers are not permitted
to stand up before Torah scholars
while they are busy with their work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story about the coin זעירי mentioned and opens a side topic about standing for scholars.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers busy at their job may not stand up for תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: But workers stand for those bringing first fruits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from the משנה in ביכורים, where all the workers stand up and greet the people bringing ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are workers really not allowed to stand? But we learned in a משנה: all the workers stand up before them, greet them, and say: Our brothers from such-and-such place, welcome!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule with a משנה that shows workers do stop to stand up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said a worker on the job does not stand. But the משנה says workers in ירושלים stand up for the people bringing ביכורים, even in the middle of work. So it seems workers may stand after all.

keyTerms.meaning: They greet them, ask how they are
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And they don't? But didn't we learn:
All the workers stand up before them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people bringing ביכורים to ירושלים (משנה ביכורים 3:3).

phrases.english: and greet them,
and say to them:
Our brothers, people of such-and-such place,
welcome!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule רבי יוחנן stated in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that workers do not stand while working
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows workers do stand up during work for those bringing ביכורים.

steps.title: They stand for ביכורים bringers, not for scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה is a special case: workers stand for the ביכורים bringers, but they do not stand for תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For them, they stand. For תלמידי חכמים, they do not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by saying the ביכורים case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not drop his rule. He agrees the workers stand for the ביכורים bringers, and says that is an exception. For תלמידי חכמים, the worker still stays seated.

keyTerms.meaning: They stand up before them (the ביכורים bringers)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: Before them, they stand;
before Torah scholars, they do not stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ביכורים משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to prove workers stand up for anyone important, including scholars.
steps.terutzMaskana: Standing for ביכורים bringers is a special case. Workers still do not stand for תלמידי חכמים while working.

steps.title: How precious a מצוה done at its time is
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין learns a lesson from this: a מצוה done at its proper time is so beloved that workers stand for the ביכורים bringers but not for scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: Come and see how beloved a מצוה is at its proper time. Workers stand up before the ביכורים bringers, but they do not stand up before תלמידי חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין draws a lesson from רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He explains why the ביכורים bringers get more honor than scholars: they are doing a מצוה right now, at its time. That makes them more honored at that moment than even a תלמיד חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see, introduces a lesson
Beloved, precious
A מצוה done at its proper time

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה חֲבִיבָה מִצְוָה בִּשְׁעָתָהּ,
phrases.english: Come and see how beloved a מצוה is at its proper time,
for before them they stand,
but before Torah scholars they do not stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה חֲבִיבָה מִצְוָה בִּשְׁעָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason and lesson based on רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה done at its time is so precious that its doers get more honor than תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: Maybe they stand only to keep them coming back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוסי בר אבין: maybe the workers stand only so the ביכורים bringers won't stop coming in future years.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know that? Maybe they stand so that you will not end up making them stumble in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבי יוסי בר אבין's proof by offering a different reason for the standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר אבין said the standing shows love for a מצוה at its time. The גמרא says there could be a practical reason: if the bringers are not warmly welcomed, they might not bother coming next year. So the standing does not prove his lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? (questions a proof)
Perhaps, offers another possibility
Making them stumble, causing them to fail
In the future

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule stands: workers do not stand for תלמידי חכמים while working, but they do stand for ביכורים bringers. רבי יוסי בר אבין said the reason is love of a מצוה at its time, but the גמרא rejects that proof: the standing may just be to keep the bringers coming back.

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps
it is so that you will not end up making them stumble
phrases.notes: If they are not warmly welcomed, they might not come to bring ביכורים next time.

phrases.english: in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the lesson רבי יוסי בר אבין drew in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבי יוסי בר אבין's reason; רבי יוחנן's distinction stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The standing could have a practical purpose, encouraging future ביכורים trips, rather than showing special love for a מצוה at its time.

steps.title: An exact measure counts as more than the measure
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that when the חכמים give a measure of a סלע or an איסר, an area exactly that size is treated as larger than it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: 'Like a סלע' means it is treated like more than a סלע. 'Like an איסר' means it is treated like more than an איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains how to treat a hole or damage that is exactly the size the חכמים gave. He says it counts as if it were bigger than that size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a hole in the windpipe is kosher up to the size of an איסר. רב נחמן teaches that a hole exactly the size of an איסר already counts as 'more than an איסר,' so the animal is a טריפה. The same rule applies to measures given as a סלע.

keyTerms.meaning: A large coin, used as a measure of size
A small coin, used as a measure of size
More than, larger than

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Like a sela means like more than a sela,
phrases.notes: He means a hole exactly the size of a סלע is already treated as bigger than a סלע.

phrases.english: like an issar means like more than an issar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כְּסֶלַע – כְּיָתֵר מִכְּסֶלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the story about רבי יוחנן and back to the measurement in our משנה (a windpipe hole the size of an איסר).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A damaged area exactly the size of a סלע or an איסר is treated as larger than that measure.

steps.title: So 'until' does not include the measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from רב נחמן's ruling that he holds 'until' means up to the measure but not including it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that רב נחמן holds: 'until' means until, but not including, the measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רב נחמן's ruling about how he reads the word 'until' in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the animal is kosher 'until' the hole is the size of an איסר. Since רב נחמן says an exact איסר counts as more than an איסר, the exact size is not part of the kosher range. So 'until' stops just before the measure itself.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see, apparently
Until, but not including, the measure itself

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not including' does not mean the exact measure is ignored. It means the exact measure falls on the other side, here the טריפה side.

phrases.english: So apparently Rav Naḥman holds:
'Until' means until, and not including the measure itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule about the word עד from רב נחמן's ruling in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב נחמן, עד means up to the measure but not including it.

steps.title: Challenge from a rope hanging off a bed
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן from a משנה that says a rope hanging off a bed is טהור 'until' five handbreadths. This suggests exactly five is still in the טהור range.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: A rope sticking out of a bed, up to five handbreadths, is טהור. Doesn't this mean that exactly five counts with the smaller amount?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a משנה that seems to use 'until' to include the measure itself. That would go against רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A short loose rope end is not counted as part of the bed, so it stays טהור. If 'until five' means a rope of exactly five is still טהור, then 'until' includes the measure. That is the opposite of רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Rope
Bed
Handbreadths (a unit of length)
Pure, not able to become impure
Doesn't it mean...? (introduces a suggested reading)
Like below, counted with the smaller amount

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Naḥman:
A rope that sticks out from the bed,
up to five handbreadths, is pure.
Doesn't it mean that five is like below?
phrases.notes: In other words, a rope of exactly five is still in the pure group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 12 that עד does not include the measure.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that עד does not include the measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in כלים seems to treat exactly five handbreadths as part of the טהור range, so there עד includes the measure.

steps.title: Exactly five counts with the larger amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a rope of exactly five handbreadths counts with the larger amount, so it is not טהור. This fits רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Exactly five is like above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's reading. It reads the משנה so that exactly five belongs to the larger, טמא group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If exactly five counts as 'above,' then 'until five' means up to but not including five. That is exactly how רב נחמן reads 'until.' So the משנה does not have to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Like above, counted with the larger amount

phrases.english: No, five is like above.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exactly five handbreadths is still in the טהור range, so עד includes the measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Exactly five counts with the larger amount, so עד does not include the measure, which fits רב נחמן.

steps.title: Second challenge from the end of the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the next line of the משנה: from five until ten is טמא. This suggests exactly ten is still in the טמא range.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: From five until ten, it is טמא. Doesn't this mean that exactly ten counts with the smaller amount?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again with the next part of the same משנה, where 'until ten' seems to include ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rope between five and ten handbreadths is useful, so it counts as part of the bed and can become טמא. If a rope of exactly ten is also in this range, then here 'until' includes the measure, against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure, or able to become impure

phrases.english: Come and hear:
From five until ten, it is impure.
Doesn't it mean that ten is like below?
phrases.notes: So a rope of exactly ten would still be in the impure group.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מֵחֲמִשָּׁה וְעַד עֲשָׂרָה – טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 answered the first line, this attacks רב נחמן again from the next line of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that עד does not include the measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'From five until ten is טמא' seems to put exactly ten in the טמא range, so עד includes the measure.

steps.title: Exactly ten counts with the larger amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a rope of exactly ten counts with the larger amount, which is outside the טמא range. This fits רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Exactly ten is like above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as before: the exact measure, ten, belongs with the larger group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If exactly ten counts as 'above ten,' then 'until ten' stops just before ten, and a rope of exactly ten is not טמא. Both lines of the משנה can be read the way רב נחמן reads 'until,' so his view stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן holds that 'until' (עד) does not include the measure, so an exact measure counts with the larger amount. Both of רבא's challenges are answered by reading the exact measure as 'above.'

phrases.english: No, ten is like above.
phrases.notes: So a rope of exactly ten is treated like a longer rope and is not impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 the same way step 14 answered step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exactly ten handbreadths is still in the טמא range, so עד includes the measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Exactly ten counts with the larger amount, so עד does not include the measure, which fits רב נחמן.

steps.title: A new משנה about tiny earthenware vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה about the smallest earthenware vessels that can stand on their own. This is setup for a new test of רב נחמן's reading of 'until'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the smallest earthenware vessels, whether the vessels themselves or their broken-off bottoms and sides, if they can sit upright without being propped up...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new source to test רב נחמן's view about 'until'. It is only setting up the case here, and the actual point comes in the next line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the test came from the rope-and-bed משנה. Now the גמרא switches to a משנה about tiny clay vessels and their broken pieces that can stand by themselves. The measurements in the rest of this משנה will be checked against רב נחמן's rule that 'until' does not include the number itself.

keyTerms.meaning: An earthenware (clay) vessel
The smallest, thinnest ones
Bottoms or bases of a vessel
Sides or walls of a vessel
Propped up or supported by something else

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the 'until' wording in this line yet. This is only the start of the משנה, and the measurement part comes next.

phrases.english: Come and hear: the smallest of earthenware vessels,
they, and their bases, and their sides,
phrases.notes: He means even broken-off pieces of the vessel, its bottom or a side wall.

phrases.english: if they sit upright without being supported –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rope-and-bed challenges were answered in steps 13–16, the גמרא brings a new משנה to test the same question about 'until'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that 'until' means up to the measure but not including it (step 12).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rest of this משנה will give measurements using 'until'. The גמרא will check whether that wording fits רב נחמן. This line only sets up the case.
